newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo no comment on report trader acted on orders.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo no comment on report trader acted on orders.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Wednesday it had no comment on a report that its former star copper trader was acting on a superior's instructions when he made his first loss-making off-the-books trade 11 years ago.

The Mainichi Shimbun newspaper said in its Wednesday evening edition that Tokyo prosecutors -- who arrested the trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, on Tuesday on suspicion of forgery -- had apparently questioned the superior and learned of his role in the 1985 loss.
It said the superior quit Sumitomo, a giant trading house, in July 1987. The paper gave no source for its report.

A Sumitomo spokesman said the trade house would not comment on the Hamanaka case while an in-house investigation was proceeding, nor would it comment on matters currently in the hands of the Tokyo prosecutors.
Tokyo prosecutors, as a matter of policy, do not comment on their investigations.

Sumitomo has said the unauthorised 1985 trade lost 6.5 billion yen and set Hamanaka on a path of ever bigger off-the-books deals as he tried to erase his losses. Despite his efforts, the company said, the losses snowballed to an estimated $2.6 billion.
Hamanaka has repeatedly refused to comment on the affair.
When Sumitomo first announced in mid-June that it had discovered massive copper trading losses, it blamed them on Hamanaka and another trader who quit the company eight years earlier.
Sumitomo fired Hamanaka in June and later filed a complaint against him, which led to Tuesday's arrest.
If convicted on the forgery charges, Hamanaka faces a prison term of three months to five years, according to a lawyer at the Japan Bar Association. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
